audit_event.notes: Per Requirement 4.3.3, recovery requires a fresh BOOTSTRAP. The new Mandate's mandate_id MUST differ from the Revoked one even when (subject, scope) match. Verifiers MUST refuse any path that reuses the old id.
audit_event.reason: REVOKE accepted; recovery via re-BOOTSTRAP yields new mandate_id

irreversibility_assertion.claim: When HP needs to restore authorisation over the same (subject, scope), the MS MUST run BOOTSTRAP again and issue a Mandate with a different mandate_id. The old id stays Revoked forever.

notes: The vector's wire pair is the REVOKE for the original Mandate; the related new Mandate's metadata (post-recovery) sits inside expected.json so verifiers can assert id disjointness without a second wire round-trip. Mandate ids MUST be globally unique even across re-bootstrap of the same (subject, scope).

signature_verification.note: REVOKE envelope is signed by HP (Requirement 4.1.3 — REVOKE auth-strength ≥ BOOTSTRAP auth-strength). REVOKE_RECEIPT / ERROR is signed by MS. Both envelopes use canonical CBOR as signing input regardless of wire encoding.

summary: Recovery after REVOKE: re-BOOTSTRAP issues a fresh Mandate with a *different* mandate_id even when (subject, scope) match. The old id remains Revoked forever. Validates Requirement 4.3.3.
